chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abi al-Maghra', from Abi Basir who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The one who forgets a Chapter from the Qur'an, it will be presented to him in a beautiful form and on an elevated level in Paradise. When he sees it, he will say: 'What are you? How beautiful you are! If only you were mine!' It will say: 'Do you not know me? I am such and such Chapter. And if you had not forgotten me, I would have elevated you to this (level).'
ai.seo_question: What happens in Paradise if a person forgets a chapter of the Qur'an?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the tangible spiritual reward of Qur'anic memorization, portraying the Surah as an intercessor that elevates the believer's rank in Jannah. It reflects the concept of the Qur'an as a living witness and companion, where neglecting its verses results in a diminished spiritual status, while consistent recitation ensures divine elevation. This narrative reinforces the practical importance of Hifz (memorization) not merely as a ritual, but as a means of securing eternal proximity to God through the Qur'an's intercession.
